body.statement: If \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)\) returns \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\), its recorded valid cover \(\mathscr C\) satisfies \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}>0\), so every same-graph pair closer than \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) is separated in a co-containing chart. Every feasible pair at least \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) apart has squared \(W\)-distance at least \(\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}>0\), with the remote claim vacuous when that pair set is empty. Therefore every \(m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}\) is globally injective on \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\), and \(Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\cdot;m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta_0))\) has unique minimum \(\theta_0\) with the certified remote separation outside its local neighborhood.
body.justification: This prevents local Jacobian rank from substituting for global uniqueness.
body.gap: A local inverse theorem alone does not certify a unique compact-box population minimum.
body.consumer: It supplies the global identification premise for the deterministic minimum-distance estimator.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\) have equal moment vectors.  If
\(\|\theta-\theta'\|_2<r_{\mathrm{id}}\), validity of the recorded cover puts them in a common chart \(C_{\boldsymbol d c}\).  Equality of moment vectors implies equality after projection, and hence
\[
0=\langle\phi_{\boldsymbol d c}(\theta)
-\phi_{\boldsymbol d c}(\theta'),\theta-\theta'\rangle
\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}\|\theta-\theta'\|_2^2.
\]
Since \(\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}>0\), this forces \(\theta=\theta'\).  If instead their distance is at least \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\), the certified remote bound gives
\[
\|m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta)
-m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta')\|_W^2
\geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}>0,
\]
contradicting equality.  When the remote set is empty this second case cannot occur.  Thus the moment map is globally injective.

For \(g_0=m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta_0)\), positive definiteness of \(W\) gives
\[
Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta;g_0)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta)=g_0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\theta=\theta_0.
\]
The displayed remote bound supplies the asserted quantitative separation outside the local neighborhood.
